The wider TMC did suffer a post-storm water-pressure crisis that nearly forced a mass evacuation (see aggregate).

events.timing: Sheltered through Sept 1, 2008 landfall; crisis peaked ~Sept 3; evacuation of remaining patients followed
events.detail: State-run charity hospital operated through the storm on generators that powered equipment but not air conditioning in the sealed building; by Wednesday the ICU reached dangerously high temperatures. An attempted switch back to grid power failed and produced smoke, and all remaining 52 patients were evacuated via the single working elevator. Primary failed-shelter-in-place case for Gustav.

events.timing: Patients evacuated before Sept 1, 2008 landfall
events.detail: Public (charity system) hospital evacuated its patients pre-landfall; Gustav's eye passage destroyed sections of the roof and damaged the electrical system, validating the evacuation decision.

events.timing: In connection with Gustav (pre- vs post-landfall not clearly documented)
events.detail: ProPublica's Gustav reporting indicates Lane Regional evacuated patients as part of the Gustav medical evacuation; whether the movement occurred pre-landfall or after the widespread post-storm power failures in East Baton Rouge Parish is not clearly established in the recovered text.

events.timing: 80 patients remained Sunday evening Aug 31, 2008, ahead of Sept 1 landfall
events.detail: Sheltered in place with 80 patients, more than half in critical-care units, deemed too fragile to move as part of the state's decision to leave some critical-care patients in facilities; New Orleans was largely spared and no post-storm evacuation of the facility was reported.

events.timing: Through Sept 1, 2008 landfall; AC out for several days afterward
events.detail: Sheltered in place; Gustav damaged the electrical substations serving the hospital and its air conditioning (not on emergency generators) was out of service for several days. No evacuation reported; the experience drove a 6-MW generator design in its replacement facility.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall Oct 10, 2018; evacuation announced Oct 11; transfers began ~3 a.m. Thu Oct 11 with 39 ICU patients first; completed over ~48 hours
events.patients_moved: ~200 announced (39 ICU); Ascension later reported 231 patients transferred total; ~1,500 people sheltered in building during storm
events.detail: 323-bed hospital sheltered ~200 patients plus staff families/first responders (~1,500 people) through Cat 5 winds; sustained roof, structural and water damage, blown-out windows, roof-section collapse over materials management building, cooling/plumbing failures and loss of information systems. Forced post-impact evacuation with HHS DMAT assistance: 103 patients to Sacred Heart Pensacola, remainder to Ascension facilities in Jacksonville FL and Mobile AL; ER stayed open on generator power.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall Oct 10; began evacuating most critical patients Thu afternoon Oct 11; reopened with limited services Nov 11, 2018
events.patients_moved: 139 (139 per WJHG; ~130 per ABC/CNN accounts)
events.detail: 238-bed HCA hospital sheltered in place, sustained significant damage and loss of public utilities (power, water, sewer), operated on full backup generator power, then evacuated 139 patients post-impact by aircraft, helicopter and ambulance to HCA sister facilities in Florida. ER never closed and treated 2,000+ patients during/after the storm; federal DMAT deployed onsite. Hospital statement: patients safest at neighboring hospitals until stable public power/water/sewage.

events.hospital: Sacred Heart Hospital on the Gulf
events.timing: Stopped new admissions Oct 7; evacuated inpatients and suspended operations Oct 9 (landfall Oct 10); resumed inpatient care Oct 19, full operations Oct 22
events.patients_moved: ~24 inpatients combined with Emerald Coast sister hospital, transferred to Sacred Heart Hospital Pensacola
events.detail: 19-bed critical access hospital ~10 miles from the Mexico Beach landfall point. Ascension/Sacred Heart Health System reduced census then evacuated all inpatients to Pensacola pre-landfall and released most staff; a skeleton facility crew rode out the storm on site. Building took only minor water-leak damage.

events.hospital: Sacred Heart Hospital on the Emerald Coast
events.timing: Evacuated remaining inpatients Oct 9, one day before landfall; resumed normal operations by Oct 11
events.patients_moved: Part of ~24 inpatients (combined with Port St. Joe facility) to Sacred Heart Hospital Pensacola
events.detail: 76-bed hospital transferred all remaining inpatients to Sacred Heart Pensacola pre-landfall; ER remained open through the storm with a skeleton crew and a relief crew standing by. Minor water-leak damage from wind-driven rain.

events.timing: Post-landfall (facility located on third floor of Bay Medical Sacred Heart campus)
events.detail: 30-bed long-term acute care hospital (LTACH) located inside the Bay Medical Sacred Heart building; listed in Florida state disaster recovery reports and Becker's as one of five Florida hospitals forced to shut down by Michael. Independent detail on its patient movement is thin; presumably evacuated alongside host hospital. Facility type: LTACH, not general acute care.

events.timing: Damage at landfall Oct 10; inpatient services closed for repairs into early spring 2019
events.detail: 86-bed psychiatric hospital (not general acute care). Storm damage forced closure of all inpatient beds for repairs; Becker's counts it among five Florida hospitals shut down, while WJHG (Jan 2, 2019) reports the facility expanded outpatient/PHP services and diverted patients needing inpatient care to Fort Walton Beach Medical Center, Baptist and West Florida Hospitals (Pensacola), Capital Regional and Tallahassee Memorial. Whether census patients were evacuated at impact is not clearly documented - recorded as UNCLEAR with both sources.

events.timing: Rode out landfall Oct 10 (inland Cat 3+ winds 130-140 mph in Jackson County); state update Oct 20 reports hospital 'has reopened and has power'
events.detail: Inland community hospital in hard-hit Jackson County. Gov. Scott's Oct 20 recovery update says the hospital 'has reopened and has power,' implying some period of closure or curtailed operations, but no contemporaneous account of a patient evacuation was found. Post-storm, FEMA approved $2.58M for 12 permanent generators for Jackson Hospital in response to Michael - indicating power vulnerability during the event. Recorded UNCLEAR pending better sourcing.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall Oct 10, 2018
events.detail: 25-bed critical access hospital. Hospital's own account states Hurricane Michael caused severe damage to the original facility 'but despite the devastation, the hospital never closed its doors.' Source is the hospital's retrospective; no contemporaneous news account located before search budget exhausted - flagged for verification.

events.timing: During/after Georgia transit of Michael, Oct 10-11, 2018
events.detail: Remained operating through the storm's inland Georgia track; had low water pressure due to a power outage but did not lose pressure entirely; among roughly a dozen Georgia hospitals on generator power per Georgia Health News.

events.hospital: Tift Regional Medical Center (reported as 'Tifton hospital')
events.timing: During/after Georgia transit of Michael, Oct 10-11, 2018
events.detail: Georgia Health News reports the Tifton hospital lost water pressure briefly but continued operating. Passing mention only.

events.timing: 1,800 staff sheltered in beginning Sept 12; landfall Sept 14 at Wrightsville Beach; remained open 24/7 while Wilmington was cut off by floodwaters for days
events.patients_moved: 8 NICU babies transferred pre-storm to WakeMed, UNC Children's Hospital, and Levine Children's Hospital; ~500 inpatients cared for in place
events.detail: Flagship documented successful shelter-in-place of Florence: cared for ~500 patients and delivered 42 babies entirely on generator power while the city was isolated by record flooding; managed ceiling leaks and stood up medical shelters at nearby schools. Pre-storm it moved its most vulnerable NICU patients inland and closed its Orthopedic Hospital campus and Scotts Hill freestanding ED (both Sept 12).

events.timing: Closed by noon Wednesday Sept 12, two days before landfall; remained closed after the storm due to flooding; Carolinas MED-1 mobile hospital arrived in Burgaw Sept 18
events.detail: Critical access hospital operated by NHRMC; evacuated/closed pre-landfall and kept closed by Northeast Cape Fear River flooding, leaving Pender County without local inpatient care for days until the 14-bed Carolinas MED-1 mobile hospital deployed from Charlotte.

events.hospital: Cape Fear Valley - Bladen County Hospital
events.timing: Evacuated Sept 11-12, 2018, pre-landfall, then closed
events.patients_moved: ~11 patients to Cape Fear Valley Health System's Hoke Hospital
events.detail: Small county hospital evacuated its full census (~11 patients) to the system's inland Hoke facility ahead of the storm and closed.

events.timing: Pre-landfall (transfers before Sept 14); ED open throughout the storm
events.patients_moved: Some patients transferred to hospitals farther inland (count not reported)
events.detail: Transferred some inpatients inland pre-storm, closed physician offices and outpatient facilities, increased staffing with staff sleeping onsite, and kept the emergency department open through the storm.

events.timing: Sheltered in place through landfall Sept 14 (Morehead City took some of the worst surge/rain); mobile medical unit deployed across the street post-storm
events.patients_moved: Most critical patients may have been transferred pre-storm (count not reported)
events.detail: 135-bed county hospital executed a planned shelter-in-place coordinated with county emergency services; doctors, nurses and administrators sheltered at the hospital, and some local nursing home patients used the hospital as refuge. A mobile medical unit set up across the street afterward to absorb demand. No forced evacuation reported.

events.timing: Sheltered through Sept 13-15 storm surge flooding of New Bern (Neuse/Trent rivers ~3 m above normal)
events.detail: 350-bed hospital remained operating while New Bern flooded catastrophically and hundreds were rescued from floodwaters; CEO described contingency plans including helicopter resupply if trucks could not get through. No evacuation reported.

events.timing: Remained operational through the storm and Lumber River flooding, Sept 14-17, 2018
events.detail: Remained open through Florence and the severe Lumberton flooding; publicly offered oxygen-dependent community members space to camp in its lobby with continuous power. No evacuation reported (in contrast to its Hurricane Matthew 2016 experience).

events.timing: Operated through landfall Sept 14 as Florence stalled over Onslow County
events.detail: Remained operating through the storm but lost inbound/outbound phone service from storm damage; floodwater damaged its education building badly enough to keep that building out of service for two years. No patient evacuation reported.

events.timing: Pre-landfall, week of Sept 10, 2018 (facility in Virginia mandatory evacuation zone)
events.patients_moved: Patients transferred to Durham VA Medical Center (count not reported)
events.detail: VA hospital in the Hampton Roads mandatory evacuation zone transferred patients to Durham VA Medical Center ahead of Florence; whether the evacuation was complete is not documented.

events.timing: Evacuation Mon afternoon Sept 10 through 11:45 p.m. Wed Sept 12 under Gov. McMaster's mandatory medical evacuation order; ER/Level I trauma center closed 8 a.m. Sept 12; hospital reopened 8 a.m. Sun Sept 16
events.patients_moved: >320 patients to more than 32 facilities in SC and across the Southeast, including nine HCA Healthcare hospitals
events.detail: HCA's 403-bed hospital fully evacuated pre-landfall in compliance with the governor's mandatory medical evacuation of coastal flood-zone hospitals - the largest single-hospital pre-landfall evacuation of Florence. Emergencies were diverted to Conway Medical Center while closed.

events.timing: Evacuated beginning Sept 11 under the Sept 10 mandatory medical evacuation order; ED services resumed Saturday Sept 15 at 10 a.m.
events.patients_moved: ~150 patients relocated across Tidelands Health facilities/system, by ambulance, medical buses and helicopter, to facilities outside the storm path
events.detail: First evacuation of the Georgetown hospital in roughly 70 years; patients initially relocated including to Tidelands Waccamaw Community Hospital and then out of the storm path. Employees sheltered in place at the facility, which leadership said could have withstood up to a Category 4; one behavioral health patient sheltered with staff because no receiving hospital could be found.

events.timing: ~Sept 26-27, 2018, roughly two weeks after landfall, ahead of forecast record crests on the Waccamaw/Pee Dee rivers at Georgetown
events.patients_moved: All currently admitted patients evacuated a second time; ER kept open
events.detail: Post-impact, storm-driven second evacuation: after reopening Sept 15, the hospital had to evacuate all admitted patients again in late September as Florence's record riverine flooding threatened Georgetown, while keeping its emergency room open. Classified POST_FSIP as a post-impact forced evacuation under the storm's degraded/flood conditions, though it was executed ahead of the forecast crest rather than after inundation.

events.timing: Evacuated beginning Sept 11 under the mandatory medical evacuation order; ED services resumed Saturday Sept 15 at 10 a.m.; outpatient locations reopened Monday Sept 17
events.patients_moved: All patients, by ambulance, medical buses and helicopter, to facilities outside the storm path (part of ~150 Tidelands patients relocated)
events.detail: Evacuated all inpatients pre-landfall under Gov. McMaster's mandatory medical evacuation of coastal flood-zone facilities; emergencies diverted toward Conway Medical Center while closed.

events.timing: Evacuated pre-landfall under the Sept 10 mandatory medical evacuation order
events.patients_moved: All patients evacuated (part of Tidelands system relocation)
events.detail: Inpatient rehabilitation hospital (not general acute care) evacuated all patients by ambulance, medical bus and helicopter along with the two Tidelands acute-care hospitals; listed among the seven SC hospitals closed under the evacuation order.

events.timing: Closed pre-landfall under the mandatory medical evacuation order (reported closed as of Sept 13-15 state updates)
events.detail: Long-term acute care hospital (LTACH, not general acute care) listed among the seven SC hospitals closed in the evacuation zone during Florence. Named-facility detail comes from state situation updates as summarized in search results; underlying page not directly retrievable - flag for verification.

events.hospital: Palmetto Behavioral Health (Palmetto Lowcountry Behavioral Health)
events.timing: Closed pre-landfall under the mandatory medical evacuation order (reported closed as of Sept 13-15 state updates)
events.detail: Psychiatric hospital (not general acute care) listed among the seven SC hospitals closed in the evacuation zone during Florence. Named-facility detail comes from state situation updates as summarized in search results; underlying page not directly retrievable - flag for verification.

events.hospital: MUSC Medical Center (Medical University of South Carolina)
events.timing: Operated through the storm; resumed normal operations Monday Sept 17, 2018
events.detail: Remained open through Florence in storm-operations mode and resumed normal operations the Monday after landfall.

events.timing: Remained open through the storm; system resumed normal operations Monday Sept 17
events.detail: Roper Hospital remained open; the system closed only its express care and physician-partner facilities that did not meet shelter-in-place requirements.

events.timing: Open through the storm; resumed normal operations Monday Sept 17
events.detail: Canceled all elective surgeries but kept its emergency rooms and hospital beds open for emergency patients through Florence.

events.timing: Open and accepting patients through landfall and the multi-week Waccamaw River flooding (statement Sept 16, 2018)
events.detail: Not in the medical evacuation zone; ED stayed open through the storm and took diverted emergencies from evacuated Grand Strand and Tidelands hospitals; reported backup generators sufficient for at least 93 hours. Suspended electives/outpatient services around Sept 17.

events.timing: Pre-landfall service reductions announced Sept 12-13, 2018
events.detail: Canceled elective surgical and outpatient testing procedures and closed physician practices ahead of the storm; disposition of inpatients (evacuated vs. sheltered) not documented in retrievable sources - recorded UNCLEAR rather than inferring shelter-in-place.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall night of Aug 23-24, 1992; water outage persisted ~1 week after
events.detail: Sheltered in place with staff and patients plus >200 near-term pregnant women housed in the auditorium; lost all electric service (switched to emergency generators) and all running water during the storm and for the following week (bottled water only, waste containers, sterile bottled water for OR scrub); 16 babies delivered during the hurricane; remained operational treating storm injuries. 81 employees resigned immediately afterward; >1,500 employee homes damaged or destroyed.

events.hospital: Homestead Hospital (former James Archer Smith Hospital)
events.timing: Closed for two weeks following Aug 24, 1992 landfall
events.detail: The hospital at ground zero of Andrew's landfall shut down for two weeks after the storm; a North Carolina National Guard unit set up a MASH field unit on the grounds to provide emergency care (babies delivered on Army cots) during the closure. Whether inpatients were evacuated pre-landfall or moved out post-impact is not documented in accessible sources - flagged for Miami Herald archive verification.

events.timing: Closed from Aug 1992 storm damage; rebuilt and reopened April 1993
events.detail: HHS OIG (Hospital Closure: 1992, OEI-04-93-00500) records that Deering Hospital 'closed due to damage as a result of Hurricane Andrew' and was rebuilt and reopened in April 1993 - an ~8-month storm-forced closure. Patient disposition during the storm (pre-evacuation vs shelter) not documented in accessible sources.

events.hospital: Jackson Memorial Hospital / Ryder Trauma Center
events.detail: Rode out the storm operational; the outer shell of the newly built Ryder Trauma Center building was ripped with chunks missing from the exterior, but the trauma center continued to treat patients and anchored the county's post-storm trauma response.

events.hospital: Leonard J. Chabert Medical Center (L.J. Chabert Hospital)
events.timing: Louisiana landfall ~1:30 a.m. Aug 26, 1992 near Morgan City; evacuation during/after impact
events.detail: The 201-bed public hospital sheltered in place; strong winds tore off part of the roof and wind-driven rain soaked the interior ($1 million damage), forcing evacuation of 70 patients under degraded post-impact conditions.

events.timing: Aug 25-26, 1992 (Andrew-spawned tornado in LaPlace)
events.detail: An Andrew-spawned tornado that ripped through LaPlace damaged the hospital's roof, and the hospital had to be evacuated - a sheltered facility forced out by structural damage.

events.hospital: Unnamed Houma hospital (infant airlift; possibly Chabert or Terrebonne General)
events.patients_moved: several infants
events.detail: Coast Guard airlifted babies from a Houma hospital after power failed there with no backup during Andrew's Louisiana landfall (photo of nurse Cathy Osterich with two evacuated babies). Facility name not given in source; may be the same event as the Chabert evacuation or a separate incident at Terrebonne General - recorded separately pending verification to avoid losing the generator-failure mechanism.

events.timing: Landfall near Wilmington Aug 26-27, 1998; evacuation forced during/immediately after roof loss
events.detail: The small hospital sheltered in place; Bonnie ripped part of the roof off (about 3,000 sq ft, plus an air conditioner), forcing evacuation of about a dozen patients under degraded conditions.

events.hospital: Lower Florida Keys Hospital (Lower Keys Medical Center)
events.timing: Inpatients and staff evacuated before Sept 25, 1998 landfall; patient evacuations halted as the storm neared
events.patients_moved: all inpatients
events.detail: Inpatients and staff were evacuated pre-landfall; a state-dispatched emergency response team (3 EM physicians, 4 EM nurses) maintained ED operations through the Category 2 landfall. 86 patients presented to the ED over 72 hours; 6 required hospitalization at the facility during the period evacuations were unavailable; the report notes four deaths during a 24-hour span (context unclear whether facility-attributed - not counted as facility deaths).

events.timing: Landfall Sept 16, 1999; Tar River flood isolation over the following days/weeks
events.detail: Sheltered in place at ~85% occupancy (621 of 731 beds; NICU at capacity with >40 infants), running on generators through power outages while Greenville's utilities (power, water, sewage plants) flooded and the city became an island. Served as the regional staging facility for Navy/National Guard helicopter rescues, chartered a Black Hawk for staff/patient transports, and ran a special-needs shelter (~26-65 people). Over 600 surgeries postponed; ~$6.2M in storm costs; 400+ employees displaced. FEMA appeal documents emergency-care standby expenses.

events.timing: Sept 16, 1999 onward (Tar River flood)
events.detail: Situated on higher ground above flooded Tarboro/Princeville, the hospital remained operational but was completely cut off by floodwaters, accessible only by helicopter.

events.timing: Sept 16, 1999 onward (Cashie River flooding)
events.detail: Became isolated by floodwaters during Floyd's flooding; no evacuation documented, but operational status details are thin - single-source entry pending corroboration from Bertie Ledger-Advance/NC DEM after-action records.

events.timing: Landfall near Cape Fear ~3 a.m. Sept 16, 1999
events.detail: Peer-reviewed first-person account (AORN Journal, 2000) documents the surgical services department's preparation for, experience during, and recovery after Floyd's direct hit on southeastern NC - the hospital rode out the storm operational.

events.timing: Sept 17, 1999 (Floyd's New England passage)
events.deaths_documented: 1 (per NCDC Climate-Watch as compiled by usdeadlyevents.com; needs primary verification)
events.detail: Outside the assigned NC/SC/VA core but same assigned storm: during Floyd's power outages the hospital's generator failed and 'one person died' per NCDC Climate-Watch (Sept 1999). No evacuation documented. Compilation-sourced; flagged for verification against the NCDC original.

events.timing: Decision Sunday morning Aug 28; buses left 1:00 p.m. and ambulances after 4:00 p.m. Sunday, ~18 hours before landfall
events.patients_moved: All inpatients: 6 sickest by ambulance (police escort) to Desoto Hospital, Mansfield LA; others by wheelchair-accessible school bus (gridlocked, rode out storm at a medically-needy shelter in Lafayette)
events.detail: The only New Orleans-area hospital to fully evacuate in advance of Katrina. Single-story building; ER reopened Monday afternoon on emergency power; inpatients returned end of week. Officials later said advance evacuation was the right call.

events.hospital: LifeCare Hospitals of New Orleans - Chalmette campus (37-bed LTACH within Chalmette Medical Center)
events.timing: Evacuated August 27, two days before landfall
events.patients_moved: All patients of 37-licensed-bed LTACH
events.detail: LifeCare Holdings' company release states its Chalmette long-term acute care hospital (leased from Universal Health Services) was evacuated on Aug 27 - a rare documented pre-landfall hospital evacuation. Its sister LifeCare units at Memorial and Kenner Regional sheltered in place.

events.timing: Sheltered through Aug 29 landfall; flooding Aug 30; generators failed Wednesday Aug 31 (accounts range from ~2 a.m. to midday); Tenet-chartered helicopters arrived Thursday Sept 1; evacuation largely complete evening Sept 1
events.patients_moved: ~187-200+ patients (LHA count 220-300 incl. LifeCare) plus ~1,800-2,000 staff/refugees; helicopter from parking-garage helipad and boats
events.deaths_documented: 45 bodies recovered Sept 11, 2005 (Tenet said 11 died before the storm); 24 of the dead were LifeCare unit patients
events.detail: The paradigm failed-shelter-in-place case: surrounded by ~10 ft of floodwater, total generator failure, 100F+ heat, no running water/sewerage. LA AG investigation (73 subpoenas, autopsies of all 45 bodies); Dr. Anna Pou arrested 2006 on 4 counts; grand jury declined to indict July 2007.

events.hospital: LifeCare Hospitals of New Orleans - Memorial campus (82-bed LTACH, 7th floor of Memorial Medical Center)
events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; 52 patients not evacuated the night after Katrina; company reported all patients/staff out by Friday Sept 2
events.patients_moved: 52 patients at time of storm
events.deaths_documented: 24 patient deaths acknowledged by Tenet as under LifeCare's care; 9 LifeCare patients found with morphine/midazolam in their systems
events.detail: Hospital-within-hospital LTACH whose ventilator-dependent patients were among the last prioritized for evacuation; the center of the euthanasia allegations investigated by the Louisiana AG.

events.hospital: Charity Hospital (Medical Center of Louisiana at New Orleans)
events.timing: Sheltered (never considered pre-evacuation - it was traditionally a receiving hospital); basement generators knocked out by flooding Tuesday morning Aug 30; ICU evacuated first; boat/helicopter evacuation repeatedly delayed (reported gunfire Thursday); completed Friday Sept 2
events.patients_moved: >350 patients (LHA count) plus ~1,200 others; final Charity+University lift ~2,200 people incl. 363 patients; 90 psychiatric patients bused to Alexandria LA; ICU patients via Tulane garage roof; 28 babies (18 NICU) among the last out
events.deaths_documented: 8 patients died during the ordeal per CEO (mostly ICU patients expected to die); morgue held 12 bodies plus 5 stacked in a stairwell; 2 Charity patients died during the Tulane-assisted evacuation; 3 terminally ill patients died during the final evacuation (Charity/University combined)
events.detail: Waist-deep water; hand-ventilation of ICU patients on the 12th floor; food ran out Wednesday; ED moved to second floor; bodies stacked in stairwell because basement morgue was full and inaccessible. Never reopened as a hospital.

events.hospital: University Hospital (Medical Center of Louisiana at New Orleans)
events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; flooded and lost power; military boats/helicopters evacuated remaining patients late Friday Sept 2
events.patients_moved: ~110 very ill patients plus ~500 staff/family/community members at the end
events.deaths_documented: See combined Charity/University counts; LSU acknowledged deaths while awaiting help
events.detail: Patients rationed to a liter of water a day; staff administered IV fluids to each other; extensive basement/first-floor flood damage; closed permanently (LSU care later resumed on USNS Comfort and in a Convention Center tent facility).

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; evacuation decision midafternoon Tuesday Aug 30 as rising water threatened generators (lost backup power evening Aug 30); helicopter evacuation from parking-garage roof Tuesday-Thursday; HCA testimony says patient evacuation completed Sept 1 (Urban Institute account says Friday)
events.patients_moved: ~180 patients (120 hospitalized during storm + 58 who arrived Sunday from the Superdome) plus ~1,000 staff/family; also lifted 38+ Charity patients ferried to its roof; HCA chartered ~24 helicopters; 11 ventilator patients, 2 on 500-lb heart pumps
events.deaths_documented: No Tulane patients died per CEO; 2 patients transferred from Charity died during the evacuation
events.detail: Corporate parent HCA arranged helicopters and receiving HCA hospitals with per-patient destinations pre-arranged - the model 'successful' post-impact evacuation. Extensive flood damage; reopened Feb 14, 2006.

events.hospital: Veterans Affairs Medical Center New Orleans
events.timing: Sheltered (code gray); by Tuesday morning no running water, >100F, elevators out (flooded basement wiring); 16 Arkansas National Guardsmen with 7 trucks arrived 9:30 p.m. Tuesday; patient movement to airport began Wednesday; main evacuation 9 a.m. Thursday Sept 1; complete Friday afternoon
events.patients_moved: ~150 patients (142 remaining at evacuation) plus ~550-700 others; trucks to Louis Armstrong airport, VA personnel airlifted to Houston
events.detail: Federal ownership brought outside help (VA Law Enforcement Training Center network); 15 critically ill patients were lifted via a Superdome heliport Tuesday. Building never reopened; replaced by new flood-hardened VA medical center with elevated generators.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; London Avenue Canal breach flooded basement and first floor (~4 ft around building) Aug 29-30; generators failed when flooding disabled a fuel pump; sickest patients airlifted from roof over following days
events.patients_moved: Most seriously ill evacuated by helicopter; corporate resupply confiscated by FEMA at the airport, then rerouted via Lafayette by helicopter
events.deaths_documented: 15-16 patients reported to have died awaiting food, fuel, generators and rescue (reported in negligence-suit coverage; LaCoste wrongful-death trial 2010)
events.detail: UHS-owned 427-bed hospital in the hardest-flooded part of the city; staff carried patients up darkened stairs to the roof; power failure left staff hand-ventilating patients. Closed permanently; site later became New Orleans East Hospital.

events.timing: Sheltered; superficial storm damage but by Monday evening Aug 29 flooding had begun, all generators failed, water pressure gone; Shreveport fire-department boats began evacuating Wednesday morning Aug 31; last patients/staff out late Thursday morning Sept 1
events.patients_moved: 120 patients boated a quarter-mile to a dry berm for helicopter lift (some to an I-10 overpass triage point); rescue team left Wednesday with 30 patients and 80 staff/family still inside overnight
events.deaths_documented: 19 bodies found; transplant surgeon on site said hospice-unit patients were dying by Tuesday from heat and dehydration
events.detail: Tenet-owned (ex-Mercy) 187-bed hospital; nurses hand-ventilated 4 ICU patients in 30-minute shifts; ran out of blood, water, most medication except morphine; ~100 vehicles submerged in its lot; 45 dogs, 15 cats and guinea pigs sheltered inside. Never reopened as an acute hospital. Deaths investigated by LA AG alongside Memorial.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall Aug 29; storm surge up the Intracoastal Waterway plus Industrial Canal levee breaches swamped the first floor with ~12 ft of water within hours; patients/staff evacuated by boat in the days after
events.patients_moved: Not reliably reported (265 licensed beds across campuses; its LifeCare LTACH unit had evacuated Aug 27)
events.detail: St. Bernard Parish's only hospital; the most severely damaged hospital building in the region per MCEER field inspection (100-mph roof damage, 12 ft brackish/oily flood, marsh grass in every opening). Never reopened; parish had no hospital until St. Bernard Parish Hospital opened 2012.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; escaped serious flooding but lost city power and water; backup generators failed even after fuel was trucked in; evacuated over the days after the storm; reopened Sept 28, 2005
events.patients_moved: 238-240 patients plus ~1,700 staff and family sheltering; half the patients left by ground in bus/car/van caravans under police guard, the rest by air; patients staged in an outdoor parking garage
events.detail: Largest non-flooded Orleans Parish hospital to be forced out by utility failure and security concerns rather than floodwater. First Orleans Parish hospital to reopen.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; escaped serious flooding but evacuated post-impact when city water pressure dropped to zero and air conditioning failed; reopened Oct 10, 2005
events.patients_moved: Patients evacuated by ambulance, helicopter, and private cars; triaged mostly to children's hospitals in Kansas and Miami with specialty-matched destinations
events.detail: CEO reported no difficulty placing patients - children's hospitals elsewhere offered more help than needed (Kansas flew doctors/nurses in). A clean example of post-impact evacuation driven purely by utility loss.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; evacuation of its 31-bed LifeCare LTACH unit (and the hospital) completed by Friday Sept 2
events.patients_moved: All patients and staff of the 31-bed LifeCare unit per company release; hospital 'gradually returned to service' after the storm
events.detail: Tenet-owned 170-bed hospital that was not flooded but closed after the storm amid region-wide power/water loss; later sold to Ochsner (2006).

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall with no flood damage; evacuated in the days after amid security collapse and utility loss; reopened Nov 6, 2005
events.patients_moved: Not reported (207 licensed beds)
events.detail: CEO Phillip Sowa: minimal law-enforcement protection for first three days, armed threats and gunfire near the hospital, harassment of a supply truck by armed bandits, gunshots aimed at a Coast Guard helicopter attempting to land; staff sent a ham-radio Mayday from the roof. MCEER records damage 'None' but status 'Evacuated' - an FSIP driven by security/infrastructure, not water.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; evacuated after the storm (reason not detailed - regional utility loss); reopened Sept 30, 2005
events.patients_moved: Not reported (102 licensed beds)
events.detail: HCA-owned suburban hospital recorded by MCEER with damage 'None', post-Katrina status 'Evacuated'; among the first to reopen.

events.timing: Open before, during, and after landfall; never evacuated
events.detail: One of only three New Orleans-area acute hospitals (with East Jefferson and West Jefferson) that stayed open through the storm and aftermath, treating all comers; sustained limited hurricane damage; posted a ~$59.5M post-hurricane operating loss.

events.timing: Open before, during, and after landfall; never evacuated
events.detail: 454-bed not-for-profit; limited hurricane damage; remained open on the east bank of Jefferson Parish (spared levee-failure flooding) and treated anyone requiring care at large financial cost.

events.timing: Open before, during, and after landfall; never evacuated
events.detail: 451-bed not-for-profit on the West Bank; spared from flooding and 'operated through the disaster's aftermath' per congressional testimony; one of the three area hospitals that never closed.

events.timing: Rode out the storm; operational in the immediate aftermath
events.detail: Northshore hospital that did not sustain serious storm damage and stayed operational despite heavy staff evacuation; covered in Sept 2005 reporting on hospitals that 'braved Katrina' and faced financial strain from uncompensated care.

Conflicting accounts: post-storm psychological-care reporting describes it (with Slidell Memorial) as not seriously damaged and operational in the aftermath, while Tenet-divestiture coverage says it 'gradually returned to service after the hurricane,' implying interruption. No account of a patient evacuation found.

events.timing: Remained open through the storm and aftermath
events.detail: HCA hospital north of Lake Pontchartrain; sustained weather/wind damage but remained open, per HCA testimony to the House hospital disaster-preparedness hearing (Jan 2006).

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall at the eyewall; storm surge flooded the first floor early Monday morning Aug 29; inpatient services lost; ED reopened Oct 5, inpatient beds Oct 28
events.patients_moved: Inpatients relocated above the surge and transferred out after the storm (count not reliably reported); staff treated ~150 people in the first 12 hours and ~800 by Thursday from improvised emergency facilities/tents
events.detail: The Mississippi hospital hardest hit by Katrina - where the eye came ashore; surge destroyed the ground floor and nearly all imaging/plant equipment (>$5M); hospital closed to inpatients for two months; staff fell from 495 to ~100 by December.

events.timing: Open throughout landfall and aftermath; lost power for only ~30 minutes
events.detail: CEO Gary Marchand: 'We never closed our doors. We never turned anyone away.' Emerged as the only fully functioning medical center on the Mississippi coast despite heavy damage reported in Gulfport; consistent with House testimony that only two hospitals functioned in the Gulfport-Biloxi area post-storm.

events.timing: Rode out the storm; resumed ER operation shortly after landfall
events.detail: HCA hospital; sustained flooding and roof damage but became one of only two functioning hospitals in the Gulfport-Biloxi area post-Katrina; FEMA installed triage/treatment tents in its parking lot (per HCA congressional testimony).

Documented as operating after the storm with catastrophic staff losses (65% of staff and 50% of physicians lost their homes; 82 staff departures by Dec 1, 2005), but House testimony that only two Gulfport-Biloxi hospitals were functioning post-storm implies degraded status; no direct account of its storm decision or any patient evacuation found.

events.timing: Sheltered at landfall Oct 29, 2012; ConEd power lost ~7:30-8:30 pm; backup generators failed by ~11 pm; evacuation ran overnight Oct 29-30
events.patients_moved: ~300 (contemporaneous reports range 215-322)
events.detail: Decided to shelter in place (had evacuated for Irene 2011); basement generator flooded and the rooftop generator's fuel pump failed, forcing an emergency nighttime evacuation down darkened stairwells - roughly 45 critical-care patients and ~20 NICU babies hand-ventilated as staff carried them down. Patients went to Mount Sinai, Memorial Sloan-Kettering, St. Luke's, NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell, and Long Island Jewish.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall Oct 29; partial evacuation began Oct 30; full evacuation/closure Oct 31, 2012
events.patients_moved: ~700+ census at landfall (ProPublica: 712); ~500 remaining patients evacuated Oct 31 after earlier transfers
events.detail: Sheltered in place; ~17 million gallons of water flooded the basement, submerging fuel pumps for the 13th-floor generator. Staff and National Guard ran a bucket brigade hauling 500 gallons of diesel up 13 flights to keep generators alive, then the hospital was fully evacuated Oct 31 under degraded conditions, with Guard troops carrying patients downstairs to ambulances; patients went to Mount Sinai and other NYC hospitals. ED partially reopened late 2012, full reopening Feb 2013.

events.timing: Ventilated patients moved 48 hrs pre-landfall, CCU patients 24 hrs pre-landfall; surge flooded the campus night of Oct 29; remaining patients evacuated starting Oct 30
events.patients_moved: 220+ evacuated post-impact (after pre-storm critical-care transfers); staff moved 28 patients to upper floors through knee-deep water during the surge
events.detail: Partial pre-landfall movement of critical patients, then sheltered ~300-bed hospital; up to 11 feet of seawater inundated the ER and campus and ground-level backup generators had to be shut down, forcing full post-impact evacuation to Brookdale, Kings County, and Maimonides. Hospital lost all power and was non-operational for months.

events.hospital: Manhattan VA Medical Center (VA NY Harbor Healthcare System)
events.timing: Evacuated Oct 28, 2012, the day before landfall
events.patients_moved: ~100-132 (American Legion: 100; ProPublica: 132)
events.detail: Full pre-landfall evacuation of the flood-zone campus; patients moved calmly by ambulance/ambulette/bus to VA facilities in Brooklyn, the Bronx, and Montrose. Campus flooded and remained closed for months; widely cited as the model pre-storm decision among Manhattan hospitals.

events.timing: Evacuated over 15 hours on Saturday Oct 27, 2012, two days pre-landfall
events.detail: Only 250-bed hospital at Manhattan's southern tip; moved 125 inpatients to other hospitals because its backup generators could run only ~42 hours if power failed; kept its emergency department open. Counted by CBS among the five NYC hospitals forced to evacuate for Sandy.

events.timing: Evacuated in predawn hours of Oct 28, 2012 (day before landfall)
events.detail: Evacuated all inpatients pre-landfall over fears the storm surge would breach Hoboken's seawall, keeping ER and OB-GYN open for emergencies; the ground floor/ED subsequently took ~4 feet of floodwater. ER reopened as urgent care within days; full reopening 13 days post-storm. NOTE: sometimes described as a failed shelter-in-place, but contemporaneous reporting documents a pre-landfall evacuation.

events.timing: Sheltered through landfall; evacuation began ~6-9 am Tuesday Oct 30, 2012
events.patients_moved: 83 (Hackensack University Medical Center received ~51)
events.detail: Hudson-riverfront hospital sheltered in place; flood damage knocked out utility power and its backup generator failed. National Guard troops transferred 83 patients out on Oct 30; although the generator was later restored, conditions were too unstable to keep patients. One of only two NJ acute-care hospitals evacuated for Sandy per the state hospital association.

events.timing: Closed as of the Oct 29, 2012 storm; exact patient-movement timing not established in sources gathered
events.detail: 162-bed barrier-island hospital: ~10 feet of water flooded the basement where all vital systems were located, destroying the plant; the hospital never reopened as an inpatient facility (NY DOH pushed merger; South Nassau later opened a freestanding ED on the site). Local/contemporaneous accounts of whether inpatients were evacuated before landfall (Nassau County barrier-island order) vs. after were not directly recoverable in this pass - flagged for follow-up in Newsday/liherald archives.

events.hospital: Staten Island University Hospital (North and South campuses, North Shore-LIJ)
events.timing: Census reduced ~50% by discharge/transfer Oct 26-28 (critically ill/ventilator patients moved out); sheltered through Oct 29 landfall
events.patients_moved: Part of ~573 patients remaining across NS-LIJ's three at-risk hospitals after pre-storm census reduction
events.detail: After fully evacuating for Irene 2011, NS-LIJ chose to shelter in place for Sandy after transferring critical-care/ventilator-dependent patients and cancelling electives. The data center lost power and floodwaters threatened the Ocean Breeze campus, but the facility held and remained operational - documented as riding out the storm.

events.timing: Critical patients transferred pre-landfall; sheltered through Oct 29 landfall
events.patients_moved: Part of ~573 patients remaining across NS-LIJ's three at-risk hospitals after pre-storm census reduction
events.detail: Sheltered in place for Sandy after pre-storm census reduction and transfer of ventilator-dependent patients. ProPublica reports water breached the vulnerable bayfront site, but the hospital was not evacuated and remained operational.

events.timing: Sheltered through Oct 29 landfall; on backup power through the week
events.detail: Documented as the only hospital left functioning in the southern third of Manhattan after Sandy, operating on backup power and bringing in two additional generators as a precaution while NYU, Bellevue, NY Downtown and the VA were dark.

events.hospital: NYU Langone Medical Center (Tisch Hospital and Rusk Institute)
events.timing: Evacuated Friday Aug 26, 2011, ahead of Aug 28 landfall, under NYC's first-ever mandatory Zone A healthcare evacuation order
events.detail: Complete pre-landfall evacuation of Tisch Hospital and Rusk Institute; dischargeable patients sent home, the rest transported to hospitals outside the flood zone; ER closed with emergencies redirected to Bellevue. The evacuation proved precautionary - Irene's surge spared the campus (contrast with Sandy 2012).

events.hospital: Manhattan VA Medical Center (VA NY Harbor Healthcare System)
events.timing: Evacuated Friday Aug 26, 2011, pre-landfall
events.detail: Columbia case study documents a steady stream of ambulance traffic evacuating Manhattan's VA medical center (alongside NYU) on Aug 26 under the Zone A order. The same campus evacuated again pre-landfall for Sandy in 2012.

events.timing: Preparations began Wednesday Aug 24; evacuation ran from early Friday Aug 26, 2011, pre-landfall
events.patients_moved: 265 (15 newborns, 2 children, 248 adults; 16 on ventilators)
events.detail: The hospital's first full-scale evacuation in its history: patients matched to beds from Manhattan to the Bronx to Brooklyn by diagnosis severity; Long Island College Hospital took ~70 evacuees. Receiving-hospital friction (unfamiliar EHR/ordering systems) caused treatment delays - an oft-cited lesson. Hospital was undamaged by Irene.

events.hospital: Staten Island University Hospital - North (Ocean Breeze campus, North Shore-LIJ)
events.timing: Evacuated Friday Aug 26, 2011, pre-landfall
events.patients_moved: Part of 947 patients across NS-LIJ's three evacuated hospitals
events.detail: One of three NS-LIJ hospitals fully evacuated pre-landfall over storm-surge risk and a '50-50' risk of sewage-plant breach; 947 patients moved system-wide with no deaths or serious injuries (Health Affairs case study). Surge reached only ~4 feet and the evacuation proved precautionary.

events.hospital: Staten Island University Hospital - South (Prince's Bay campus, North Shore-LIJ)
events.timing: Evacuated Friday Aug 26, 2011, pre-landfall
events.patients_moved: Part of 947 patients across NS-LIJ's three evacuated hospitals
events.detail: Second SIUH campus fully evacuated pre-landfall as part of NS-LIJ's 947-patient, three-hospital evacuation completed without deaths or serious injuries.

events.timing: Phased evacuation beginning evening of Aug 26, completed midday Aug 27, 2011, pre-landfall
events.patients_moved: Part of 947 patients across NS-LIJ's three evacuated hospitals
events.detail: Fully evacuated pre-landfall as the third NS-LIJ at-risk hospital; the storm's below-forecast surge later fueled internal debate about whether the evacuation had been necessary - directly shaping NS-LIJ's decision to shelter in place for Sandy in 2012.

events.hospital: Good Samaritan Hospital Medical Center (Catholic Health Services)
events.timing: Evacuated Friday-Saturday Aug 26-27, 2011 (all patients out within 24 hours), pre-landfall
events.patients_moved: 370 (~170 discharged home, ~200 transferred)
events.detail: South-shore Suffolk County hospital fully evacuated pre-landfall; transfers went to five Catholic Health Services sister hospitals plus Winthrop University Hospital and Stony Brook University Hospital. No physical plant damage; operations back to normal by Aug 30.

events.timing: Evacuated by the Aug 27, 2011 5 pm Rockaway deadline, pre-landfall
events.detail: Local paper The Wave reported 'Both hospitals were evacuated as were numerous nursing and adult homes on the peninsula' under Bloomberg's expanded Rockaway evacuation order; Peninsula Hospital Center was one of the peninsula's two hospitals (it closed permanently in early 2012 for unrelated financial reasons, before Sandy). Named-facility confirmation is inferential from the two-hospital geography - flagged LOW.

events.timing: Evacuated by the Aug 27, 2011 5 pm Rockaway deadline, pre-landfall
events.detail: Second of the Rockaway peninsula's two hospitals covered by The Wave's 'Both hospitals were evacuated' report under the mandatory Rockaway order. Named-facility confirmation inferential from geography - flagged LOW.

events.timing: Zone A mandatory evacuation deadline 8 pm Aug 27, 2011
events.detail: Widely referenced as having evacuated for Irene under the Zone A order (it sat in Zone A and demonstrably pre-evacuated for Sandy in 2012), but the primary pages that would confirm the 2011 event (NYC mayoral releases pr308-11/pr311-11, NYC DOH retrospective PDF) returned HTTP 403 in this pass and no directly verifiable contemporaneous account was captured. Needs manual archive verification.

events.timing: Remained open through Aug 27-28, 2011
events.detail: Explicitly documented as remaining open on higher ground during Irene, absorbing emergency patients diverted from NYU Langone's closed ER. (Its Sandy 2012 experience a year later was the opposite.)

events.hospital: AtlantiCare Regional Medical Center - City Campus
events.timing: Sheltered through Irene's Aug 28, 2011 landfall near Atlantic City
events.patients_moved: ~130 maintained in-house (not evacuated)
events.detail: Despite Atlantic City's mandatory citywide evacuation, the hospital sheltered in place with ~130 patients after cancelling elective surgeries across the AtlantiCare system to shrink its census; rode out the storm at the landfall point.

events.timing: Through Irene's Aug 27-28, 2011 passage over coastal Delaware
events.detail: Documented as keeping its Emergency Department, operating rooms, and Labor and Delivery fully staffed and ready throughout the storm despite Sussex County coastal evacuations; inpatient and most outpatient services open by Monday Aug 29. No evacuation reported in Delaware (per contemporaneous state roundups).

events.timing: During Irene's Aug 27, 2011 NC landfall (Cape Lookout, ~30 mi away)
events.detail: CNN's state-by-state Irene coverage reported a hospital in Morehead City running on generators during the storm while remaining in operation; Carteret General was Morehead City's only hospital. Facility name is inferred from geography - flagged LOW. No pre-landfall hospital evacuations were documented anywhere in coastal NC for Irene in this pass (mandatory orders covered residents/visitors, not hospitals).

events.hospital: Vermont State Hospital (state psychiatric hospital - NOT acute care; include/exclude per protocol)
events.timing: Flooded the night of Aug 28, 2011 as Irene's remnants pushed the Winooski River over its banks; evacuated that night under emergency conditions
events.detail: First evacuation in the 120-year-old facility's history: staff moved 51 involuntarily-committed psychiatric patients out of the flooding Waterbury complex at night, scattering them to facilities statewide. The hospital never reopened - Gov. Shumlin closed it permanently, collapsing Vermont's inpatient psychiatric capacity for years. Flagged: psychiatric hospital, not an acute-care general hospital - registry team should decide inclusion.
Sheltered in place through Cat 3 landfall; lost utility power at 2:30pm on landfall day (July 10) and ran on backup generators with a stated 60-hour fuel capacity. No evacuation reported.
events.timing: Landfall July 10, 2005 ~2:25pm CDT; power lost 2:30pm

events.detail: Military acute-care hospital sheltered in place with the eye coming ashore ~25 miles east; sustained only minor damage per Navy news service. No patient evacuation reported.
events.timing: Landfall July 10, 2005

events.hospital: Baptist Hospital (and Gulf Breeze Hospital), Baptist Health Care
events.detail: System's own history states all Baptist Health Care hospitals 'remained in operation throughout the storm and as the area recovered' less than a year after Ivan. Retrospective self-report; no contemporaneous corroboration found.
events.timing: Landfall July 10, 2005

events.detail: Evacuated its 8 inpatients the Saturday before landfall; some patients sent to the Florida mainland and as far as Alabama.
events.timing: Saturday Oct 22, 2005; landfall Oct 24

events.hospital: West Boca Medical Center (West Boca Hospital)
events.detail: Sheltered through the storm, then evacuated 36 newborns after Wilma passed amid hospital damage/power loss; one of at least three FL hospitals that moved patients out post-impact.
events.timing: After Oct 24, 2005 landfall
events.patients_moved: 36 newborns

events.hospital: Kindred Hospital Fort Lauderdale (long-term acute care)
events.detail: Post-storm generator failure forced transfer of roughly 35 ventilator-dependent patients to other facilities.
events.timing: Days after Oct 24, 2005 landfall
events.patients_moved: ~35 ventilator patients

events.detail: 145-bed causeway hospital fully evacuated pre-landfall; reports of 64+ patients moved by 22 ambulances Wednesday Oct 5 (NBC reported 90+ moved since Tuesday). Conflicting counts, consistent full evacuation.
events.timing: Oct 4-5, 2016, ~2 days before closest approach Oct 7

events.detail: ~50 inpatient-rehab and transitional-care patients moved Oct 5 to Florida Hospital Memorial Medical Center in Daytona Beach; ED closed.
events.timing: Wednesday Oct 5, 2016

events.hospital: Florida Hospital New Smyrna (former Bert Fish Medical Center)
events.detail: 24 patients and 40 staff evacuated to Florida Hospital Fish Memorial (Orange City); ED closed for the storm.
All inpatients evacuated pre-storm; emergency department remained open for emergencies.
Explicitly not evacuated; received evacuees from sister coastal campuses (Oceanside) and kept ED open through the storm.
Closed for the storm as a coastal campus; still closed Saturday Oct 8 pending safety assessment before reopening.
events.timing: Closed pre-landfall; assessed Oct 8, 2016

events.detail: Closed for the storm; remained closed Saturday afternoon pending assessment before reopening.
events.timing: Closed pre-landfall; assessed Oct 8, 2016

events.hospital: Southeast Georgia Health System - Brunswick Campus
events.detail: ~180 patients evacuated early Friday Oct 7 to facilities in Georgia and Florida ahead of Matthew's closest approach; subject of a peer-reviewed case study on the economic impact of coastal-hospital hurricane evacuations.
events.timing: Early Friday Oct 7, 2016

events.hospital: Southeast Georgia Health System - Camden Campus
events.detail: Camden County hospital closed and evacuated pre-landfall; patients transferred to UF Health North (Jacksonville) and inland Georgia hospitals (Tift Regional, Cook Medical Center).
Level 1 trauma center explicitly did not evacuate patients; clinical staff plus ~100 law enforcement officers and paramedics remained on site through the storm.
Evacuated ~62 patients Friday morning ahead of the storm to inland facilities in Aiken, Dillon and Cheraw; emergency room closed.
events.timing: Friday morning Oct 7, 2016

events.detail: Downtown Charleston academic medical center publicly stated it had no plans to evacuate its ~550 patients and sheltered in place through landfall.
events.timing: Oct 7-8, 2016; SC landfall Oct 8

events.detail: Sheltered through the storm, then Lumberton's flooded water plant left the hospital without municipal water for ~9 days and a backup generator failed the following Wednesday; 'many critical-needs patients' were evacuated post-impact while the hospital stayed open on tanker water, a temporary water treatment plant, manual fire watch, and a state-supplied generator.
events.timing: Storm Oct 8; water plant flooded Oct 10; partial evacuation Wednesday Oct 12, 2016
events.patients_moved: unspecified 'many critical-needs patients'

events.detail: During Hermine's approach, a lightning strike ignited a generator-room/roof fire that knocked out power to most of the hospital, forcing its first-ever full evacuation: all 209 patients (12 critical first) carried down stairs to ambulances and distributed to Tampa Bay-area hospitals. Storm-driven electrical failure, though evacuation occurred before landfall (Sept 2 at St. Marks).
events.timing: Fire and evacuation Aug 31-Sep 1, 2016; Hermine landfall Sep 2

events.detail: Largest hospital in SW Louisiana sheltered in place through Cat 4 landfall (including 19 NICU babies consolidated from its Women's campus), then evacuated all 146 patients beginning the day after landfall because the city water system was destroyed (no water for sterilization or AC) while running on generators; ER kept open to treat-and-transfer. Patients dispersed to facilities across Louisiana.
events.timing: Landfall ~1am Aug 27, 2020; evacuation Aug 27-28

events.hospital: Lake Charles Memorial Hospital for Women
events.detail: NICU with 19 babies evacuated pre-landfall to the main Lake Charles Memorial campus (moved in under two hours) due to flood threat at the Women's campus; post-storm the babies were transferred out of the region (10 to Our Lady of Lourdes Women's & Children's, Lafayette; others elsewhere).
events.timing: Pre-landfall move Aug 26, 2020; out-of-region transfers Aug 27+
events.patients_moved: 19 NICU infants

events.detail: Ride-out teams sheltered with patients through landfall; hospital sustained roof, skybridge and window damage and operated on backup power and a secondary water supply; after surveying damage it transferred patients out post-storm, including 4 NICU babies to CHRISTUS Southeast Texas St. Elizabeth, with 48 adult/NICU patients from the CHRISTUS Lake Charles hospitals taken by Ochsner facilities.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 27, 2020; transfers over following ~48 hours
events.patients_moved: 48 (combined CHRISTUS Lake Charles transfers to Ochsner) + 4 NICU to Texas

events.detail: Sheltered through landfall, then transferred patients post-storm to other CHRISTUS and Ochsner facilities as part of the 48-patient CHRISTUS Lake Charles movement amid the citywide water/power outage.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 27, 2020; transfers Aug 27-29
events.patients_moved: included in 48 combined

events.detail: Sheltered through the storm but sustained wind damage outside and water/other damage inside; hospital and urgent care closed to routine services for days post-storm. No patient evacuation reported.
events.timing: Landfall Sep 16, 2020 (Gulf Shores AL); closures reported Sep 17-18

events.detail: Ochsner preemptively evacuated this smaller hospital on Sunday morning before landfall after the track shifted east; 35 patients moved to three other regional hospitals in under three hours.
events.timing: Sunday morning Aug 29, 2021, hours before landfall

events.detail: Sheltered through Cat 4 landfall; elevator penthouse blown off and water intrusion; ~30 patients evacuated early Monday (part of ~60 from two bayou hospitals, and of 165 Ochsner moved Monday) to other Ochsner facilities.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 29, 2021; evacuation early Aug 30

events.detail: Sheltered through landfall; storm damage forced evacuation of ~30 patients early Monday to other Ochsner facilities while the emergency room remained open.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 29, 2021; evacuation early Aug 30

events.detail: Sheltered through landfall near the point of maximum winds; sustained significant roof damage and lost air conditioning; ~100 patients transferred post-storm with Ochsner system assistance to Baton Rouge, New Orleans, Morgan City and elsewhere.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 29, 2021; transfers Aug 30-31

events.hospital: Lady of the Sea General Hospital
events.detail: Critical-access hospital sheltered in place near the landfall point; part of the roof blew off during the storm (no injuries); U.S. Coast Guard flew in Monday morning and evacuated about 7 patients. Facility sustained significant damage.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 29, 2021; Coast Guard evacuation morning of Aug 30

events.detail: Sheltered in place; reported a partial generator failure to the state during the storm — ICU ventilators lost power and staff manually bagged patients while moving them to another floor. Hospital did not lose all critical power and no off-site evacuation was documented; accounts differ on severity (NBC: ventilators stopped, manual ventilation; state: partial generator failure, patients relocated internally).
events.timing: Night of Aug 29-30, 2021
events.patients_moved: internal relocation only

events.detail: Sheltered in place; part of the roof tore off during the storm and workers sheltered in a hallway per a staff nurse, but the hospital was not reported to have evacuated patients.

events.hospital: Ochsner Medical Center (Jefferson Highway main campus)
events.detail: Flagship campus and other New Orleans Ochsner facilities stayed fully open through the storm despite rooftop ventilation covers blown off, a few broken windows (two patient rooms) and interior water leaks; served as receiving site for bayou-hospital evacuees.
Shut down and evacuated pre-landfall due to storm-surge threat; patients ferried by ambulance to other HCA facilities. Back near full operations within ~24 hours post-storm.
events.timing: Aug 28-29, 2023; landfall Aug 30 at Keaton Beach

events.detail: Closed and evacuated pre-landfall; patients transferred by ambulance to other HCA facilities.
Closed and evacuated pre-landfall; patients transferred by ambulance to other HCA facilities.
Evacuated more than 60 patients pre-landfall to other AdventHealth facilities due to surge threat on the Anclote River.

The only hospital in the landfall county proactively moved all inpatients to other facilities before the Cat 3 landfall while keeping its emergency department open; reopened/operational after the storm.
events.timing: Aug 29, 2023; landfall Aug 30 ~10 miles away at Keaton Beach
events.patients_moved: all inpatients (count not reported)

events.detail: Islanded Level 1 trauma center deployed its AquaFence flood barrier and sheltered in place rather than evacuate as Idalia's surge threatened Tampa Bay; no evacuation occurred.
events.timing: Barrier deployed Aug 28-29, 2023

events.hospital: Memorial Hermann Hospital and Memorial Hermann Children's Hospital (Texas Medical Center)
events.detail: Sheltered in place through Allison's stalled rains; overnight June 8-9 floodwater from Brays Bayou filled two lower levels via the TMC tunnel network, submerging switchgear and backup generators. Hospital lost all power, water, communications, elevators and essential services; ventilator patients were hand-bagged and carried down 10 flights on backboards. Of 575 inpatients, 169 had been discharged pre-storm; the remaining 406 were evacuated post-impact over ~31 hours to area hospitals by ambulance and helicopter (including Army Black Hawks, roof evacuations). First total evacuation/closure in the hospital's 76-year history; closed to patient care for 38 days.
events.timing: Flooding and generator failure overnight June 8-9, 2001; evacuation began June 9 and required ~31 hours
events.patients_moved: 406 evacuated post-impact (575 census minus 169 pre-storm discharges); contemporaneous press reported ~540-600 including NICU, burn and trauma patients

events.detail: Sheltered in place under severely degraded conditions: lost utility power and functioning emergency generators; ventilators inoperable, so physicians and nurses hand-bagged ventilator-dependent patients in relays (Dr. Kenneth Mattox was in charge that night). Hospital did not evacuate as a facility; accounts indicate some ventilated patients were bagged 'until they could be transported.'
events.timing: Night of June 8-9, 2001

events.hospital: St. Luke's Episcopal Hospital (Texas Medical Center)
events.detail: Rode out the flood in place with basement flooding losses similar to neighboring TMC institutions; employees formed a human chain in the stairwell of the 23-story hospital to pass food and supplies to floors after elevators were lost. No patient evacuation reported.
events.timing: June 8-9, 2001 and aftermath

events.detail: 208-bed hospital sheltered in place at landfall and took a direct hit: windows blown out, part of roof blown off, no power or phone service. Treated ~50 storm casualties (crush injuries) in the damaged building, then evacuated ALL patients the day after landfall; more than 200 ambulances (many from southeast Florida) plus Coast Guard helicopters moved patients to hospitals in Orlando, Sarasota, Tampa and Lee County. Operations suspended; ER reopened in under a week, then partial operations. CNO quote: 'We really have to get the patients out of here. This place just isn't safe.'
events.timing: Landfall ~3:45 pm Aug 13, 2004; full evacuation carried out Aug 14
events.patients_moved: All inpatients (exact count not reported) plus ~50 storm casualties triaged

events.hospital: Bon Secours-St. Joseph Hospital (renamed Peace River Regional Medical Center in 2005)
events.detail: Sheltered in place; Charley's winds blew off the roof and metal wall-panel failure at an elevator penthouse destroyed elevator control equipment. Four nursing floors were evacuated and patients were moved to other hospitals after the storm.
events.timing: Damage at landfall Aug 13, 2004; patient movement post-impact
events.patients_moved: Four nursing floors (count not reported)

events.detail: Roof blown off by Charley's winds (NCDC-sourced Wikipedia claim; corroborated by a Fawcett nurse's retrospective account) and counted among the 'three Charlotte County hospitals out of commission' per local officials, but no explicit contemporaneous account of whether inpatients were evacuated off-site was recovered. Record as damaged-status-unclear pending Charlotte Sun/AHCA archive pull.
events.timing: Landfall Aug 13, 2004

events.detail: Sheltered in place directly in Charley's inland path; part of the roof peeled back exposing patients and critical equipment to wind-driven rain, and 35+ windows shattered (~$2.3M damage). Staff maintained operations through the storm and handled 3x normal ER volume, but the hospital was closed except for the emergency room and inpatients were evacuated to other hospitals after Charley passed.
events.timing: Storm passed Aug 13, 2004; inpatient evacuation after passage

events.detail: Landfall-point hospital executed a pre-landfall partial evacuation: moved out 110 of its ~250 inpatients, routing the majority to Tampa hospitals and to the system's smaller, less vulnerable south hospital, while keeping the sickest (ventilator-dependent and too-frail) patients. During the storm a tornado tore off chunks of the roof, all five elevators flooded and the sixth floor flooded; staff moved patients down stairwells to lower floors using blankets as stretchers. DMATs deployed to the system afterward.
events.timing: Transfers Sept 2-4; landfall 12:30-1:00 am Sept 5, 2004 at Sewall's Point/Hutchinson Island
events.patients_moved: 110 of ~250 pre-landfall

events.detail: The system's southern, less exposed hospital sheltered in place and absorbed patients routed from the north hospital; in the days after Frances, FEMA DMATs operated a mobile medical center outside the south hospital to assist with surging patient care. Staff family members were sheltered in-hospital with pre-registration wristbands.

events.hospital: Miami Children's Hospital (now Nicklaus Children's Hospital)
events.detail: Explicitly documented successful shelter-in-place: its $11.3M hurricane-resistant shell retrofit (completed spring 2004) meant young patients and families did not need to evacuate when Frances struck; the hospital sheltered nearly 1,000 staff and family members during Frances and during the season hosted 60+ ventilator/electrically-dependent children evacuated from the Florida Keys.

Evacuated and suspended services ahead of Hurricane Ivan's projected Keys passage, per owner Health Management Associates' contemporaneous press release ('evacuated and have suspended services until after Hurricane Ivan passes').
events.timing: ~Sept 10-13, 2004, pre-landfall (Ivan passed west of the Keys Sept 14-15)

events.detail: Evacuated and suspended services ahead of Hurricane Ivan, per Health Management Associates' contemporaneous press release. Some of the Keys' evacuated ventilator-dependent pediatric patients were received at Miami Children's Hospital during the 2004 season.
events.timing: ~Sept 10-13, 2004, pre-landfall

events.detail: Documented ride-out: at ~2 am Sept 16 Ivan's ~130-mph winds battered the boarded-up windows, knocked out utility electricity and forced operation on emergency generators, which held. Staff pre-positioned before landfall anticipating impassable roads; more than 2,000 family members of patients and staff were sheltered in the hospital. Damage to the campus was reported in Gov. Jeb Bush's first post-landfall briefing, but the hospital and patients came through without evacuation.
events.timing: Landfall ~2 am CDT Sept 16, 2004

events.detail: Damaged (named in Gov. Jeb Bush's Sept 16 briefing as among damaged Pensacola hospitals), but Baptist Health Care's own account states all of its hospitals (Baptist, Gulf Breeze, Jay, Atmore Community) 'remained in operation throughout the storm and as the area recovered.' No evacuation documented.

Sheltered in place; named among damaged Pensacola hospitals in Gov. Bush's first briefing. Sustained water damage requiring extended drying operations (hoses pumping hot air), but no patient evacuation was reported.
events.timing: Sept 16, 2004 and aftermath

events.detail: System-level claim only: Baptist Health Care states all its hospitals remained in operation throughout Ivan; Gulf Breeze sits on the peninsula between Pensacola Bay and Santa Rosa Sound in the hardest-hit surge zone. No facility-specific account recovered.

System-level claim only: Baptist Health Care states all its hospitals, including rural Jay Hospital in Ivan's inland eyewall path through Santa Rosa County, remained in operation throughout the storm. No facility-specific account recovered.

For the second direct hit in three weeks, Martin Memorial again reduced census and routed the majority of patients to Tampa or the system's south hospital pre-landfall (its A-Team was deliberately scaled down given low in-hospital census). During Jeanne the north hospital lost part of its roof with water leaking in; dozens of patients were relocated to other floors internally, with no injuries reported and no off-site evacuation.
events.timing: Pre-landfall reduction Sept 24-25; landfall ~midnight Sept 25-26, 2004 near Sewall's Point
events.patients_moved: Dozens relocated internally; pre-landfall transfer count not reported

events.hospital: Miami Children's Hospital (now Nicklaus Children's Hospital)
events.detail: Documented as not needing to evacuate patients when Jeanne struck, credited to the hurricane-resistant shell retrofit completed spring 2004.

aggregates.claim: 16 hospitals from central to southwestern Florida evacuated or were in the process of evacuating as of Thursday afternoon Sept 29, 2022, per Florida Hospital Association president/CEO Mary Mayhew; about 1,000 patients evacuated from hospitals across five counties

AHCA Secretary Simone Marstiller reported ~350 hospital patients evacuated statewide as of early afternoon Wed Sept 28 (landfall day), alongside 3,508 residents from 40 nursing homes and 3,012 residents from 91 ALFs (AP figures; the same AP reporting counted 15 hospitals having evacuated patients)

At least 9 hospitals in southwest Florida were without potable water and more than 1,200 patients were being evacuated from hospitals lacking water, per Florida Hospital Association (AP, Sept 29-30, 2022)
Three Lee County hospitals without running water held nearly 900 patients among them (NBC News, early October 2022)
Nearly 9,000 patients and residents were evacuated from more than 200 health care facilities of all types statewide (hospitals, nursing homes, ALFs)
Lee Health transferred roughly 400 patients out of its hospitals post-storm due to loss of running water, per AHCA and Lee Health; transfers halted Oct 4 when water pressure was restored

11 health care facilities had evacuated across Osceola, Palm Beach, Miami-Dade and Volusia counties as of Thursday morning Nov 10, 2022 (facility types unspecified; no hospitals named), per Florida Division of Emergency Management; AHCA activated Health Facility Reporting System for census/evacuation/generator status
2 health care facilities reported operating on generator power as of Saturday morning Nov 12, 2022, per Florida Division of Emergency Management

AHCA final tally: 401 healthcare facilities evacuated ahead of Milton - 21 hospitals, 8 freestanding hospital EDs, 76 nursing homes, 223 assisted living facilities - the largest healthcare evacuation in Florida history

Pre-landfall interim AHCA count: over 350 healthcare facilities including 16 hospitals and 7 freestanding EDs had evacuated (a companion report: 23 hospitals and freestanding hospital EDs had initiated evacuations)

State officials (Tue Oct 8 / Wed Oct 9): 10 hospitals reporting evacuations, ~300 healthcare facilities total, 63 nursing homes, 169 ALFs, 5,000-6,000 nursing home residents moved using ~600 vehicles; blue wristbands tracked origin/destination
Pinellas County's mandatory evacuation order (zones A-C) covered 6 hospitals, 25 nursing homes, and 44 ALFs totaling ~6,600 patients
HCA Florida transferred ~400 patients by air and ground from 5 evacuating hospitals (Pasadena, Largo West, West Tampa, Englewood, Fawcett) to sister facilities

Florida Hospital Association CEO Mary Mayhew: 8 Florida hospitals evacuated and transferred patients ahead of Helene; Becker's named St. Petersburg, South Tampa, West Tampa, and Pasadena hospitals (all HCA) among them, plus 4 hospitals that switched to backup generators the night of Sept 26
CONFLICTING lower count: AP reported only 6 of Florida's 300+ hospitals had to evacuate for Helene (vs. FHA's 8) - both counts retained pending AHCA records
Ballad Health evacuated two additional hospitals (incl. Sycamore Shoals) and one nursing home by ambulance within 24 hours of the Unicoi County Hospital rooftop rescue; none sustained damage
Only 20 Texas hospitals closed or evacuated statewide despite the storm's size, per the Texas Hospital Association's after-action Special Report.

SETRAC (SouthEast Texas Regional Advisory Council): ~1,500 patients evacuated from Houston-area hospitals; nearly two dozen hospitals evacuated patients by ambulance and airplane to Dallas, San Antonio, Austin and Waco; roughly 25 hospitals declared internal disaster status; no Houston-area hospital shuttered permanently by the flooding itself (as of Aug 30, 2017).
About two dozen Houston-area hospitals remained closed as of midafternoon Aug 30, 2017, but most hospitals were up and fully functional (SETRAC via NPR).
HHS helped evacuate 182 patients from three hospitals in Victoria, Texas (Citizens Medical Center, DeTar Navarro, DeTar North) after the city lost power and water.
At least 35 hospitals across Florida, Georgia and South Carolina closed entirely or ordered partial evacuations in advance of Irma (STAT tally, Sep 9, 2017).
Florida Hospital Association: health care facilities had evacuated nearly 1,900 patients as of Sep 9, 2017, while the vast majority of its 200+ member hospitals remained open.
Florida Department of Health: more than 435 health care centers evacuated for Irma, including 30 hospitals, 61 nursing homes and 280 assisted-living facilities.
Florida Governor's office post-storm update: more than 100 assisted living facilities, 10 hospitals, and 99 other health care facilities (including 40 nursing homes) evacuated or closed.
Just 10 of Florida's 300+ hospitals closed due to the storm; 150 of 700 nursing homes lacked full power three days after Irma (NPR, Sep 19, 2017).
HCA Inc. evacuated four hospitals in the Houston area ahead of Rita (names not given); company reported all were in good shape and would reopen within days

The Texas Medical Center's 13 hospitals (Houston) planned to remain open / shelter in place through Rita; one flood-vulnerable Memorial Hermann system hospital began pre-landfall patient evacuations to sister Hermann hospitals
Military cargo planes evacuated hundreds of medical patients and others from Beaumont before landfall (Sept 22-23, 2005)
Contemporaneous reporting: Houston-area 'hospitals and nursing homes were emptied' ahead of landfall, applying Katrina lessons

Peer-reviewed study of one hospital system: 7 of 10 eligible hospitals evacuated due to Rita; EOPs activated mean 85 hrs pre-landfall, evacuation decision ~30 hrs after activation, execution ~22 hrs; 5 hospitals lost power mean 4.8 days (range 0.5-11); 3 fully-evacuated hospitals ran 40-60% understaffed; EDs kept receiving patients during evacuation

~107 evacuation-related deaths statewide, including 23 nursing-home residents in the I-45 bus fire and 10 deaths during evacuations of chronic health facilities (Houston Chronicle identified 18 more nursing-home deaths); none identified in sources as acute-care hospital inpatients

~10,000 hospital, nursing home, and home-based special-needs patients evacuated pre-storm by plane, helicopter, bus, car, ambulance, and train - described as the largest pre-storm medical evacuation in American history

Louisiana officials (Tuesday Sept 2): almost 700 patients in a dozen Louisiana hospitals might need evacuation over the following three days because facilities lacked air conditioning; 139 patients in serious condition already evacuated post-storm by Tuesday evening

At least 40 Louisiana hospitals were operating on generator power on Thursday Sept 4, most without air conditioning; dozens of hospitals and nursing homes lost power and were partially or fully evacuated post-storm when 'safe harbor' Baton Rouge was hit harder than New Orleans
Of the first 18 storm-attributed deaths in Louisiana (by Wednesday Sept 3), eight were medical evacuees
NDMS moved 225 patients from Louisiana hospitals to 12 hospitals in central Arkansas on Aug 31, 2008; ~500 patients were evacuated through Louisiana's Medical Institution Evacuation Plan (MIEP)
20 of 170 hospitals across the impacted region sustained severe damage and 17 hospitals required evacuation (CMAJ news report)

Post-storm loss of municipal water pressure at the Texas Medical Center (Houston) 'almost resulted in one of the largest patient evacuations in history' - hospitals were down to ~24 hours of patient services before pressure was restored
Eight hospitals evacuated patients in the wake of Hurricane Michael, although five of those remained open for emergency patients (per Florida AHCA, reported Oct 12, 2018)

More than 30 health-care facilities (hospitals plus nursing homes and other regulated facilities) had to be evacuated, and several small critical-access hospitals were evacuated before landfall - AHCA Secretary Justin Senior / state emergency management officials, Oct 12, 2018
Florida CFO Jimmy Patronis estimated 'approximately 10 hospitals that are going to have to be evacuated' (Oct 12, 2018, contemporaneous estimate; conflicts with AHCA's count of 8)
Georgia Gov. Nathan Deal: 35 hospitals or nursing homes in Georgia out of power and running on generators after Michael's inland track (Oct 11-12, 2018)
